question: Q5: Where do standard diagnostics and the CD observable disagree?
dataset: THEMIS-A Oct 27 - Nov 2 2008, curated Zenodo V2 magnetopause crossings

likely_causes: Partial/grazing magnetopause crossings without full boundary transition
Low-rotation crossings: |B| magnitude changes but direction preserved
Slow crossings: transition timescale exceeds embedding window (~8 min for 32D)
Pre-disrupted intervals: already disordered, no further spike at boundary
Tangential discontinuities (TDs) in magnetosheath -- sharp rotation, not boundary
Embedded current sheets -- phase coupling breaks without region change
Flux transfer events (FTEs) -- localized reconnection signatures
Mirror mode / compressive structures (consistent with Q2 r=-0.245)
Bow shock vicinity structure -- curated list is magnetopause-only

key_insight: The 11% false negative rate (13 missed of 118) means the associator is insensitive to partial/grazing crossings where phase coupling is not fully disrupted. The 16.7% false alarm rate means the associator detects ~6 additional phase-geometry transitions per week that are real magnetic structures but not magnetopause crossings. These are likely TDs, FTEs, and mirror modes.
connection_to_q1: Q1 showed phase coupling suppresses the associator. False negatives are crossings where coupling was already low (no spike). False alarms are non-boundary events where coupling breaks temporarily.
connection_to_q2: Q2 showed compressive modes correlate with higher associator. False alarm transitions likely coincide with compressive/mirror mode activity in the magnetosheath.
